subject: Overage settlement & next steps for Q4 retroactive usage
messages:
From: FinPay Billing <billing@finpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice question: unexpected overage on 2026-02-28 invoice

Hi Rafael,

We reviewed invoice Inv_2026-02-28 and noticed a $42,150 one-time overage charge labelled 'Q4 retrospective usage adjustment'. This came after we submitted our monthly usage reports and we don't recall agreeing to a retroactive true-up at that level.

Can you share a line-by-line breakdown (by model, tokens, and date) and point us to the contract clause that authorizes retroactive billing? If possible we'd prefer to convert this into a committed capacity add-on or receive a credit instead of a one-time charge.

Attached: FinPay_Q4_usage_export.csv; Inv_2026-02-28.pdf

Thanks,
Ayesha Khan
Director, Finance — FinPay
procurement@finpay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question: unexpected overage on 2026-02-28 invoice

Hi Ayesha — thanks for flagging this. I received the invoice and usage export OK. I'm looping in our CS and finance leads to validate the calculations and look at options (credit vs. commitment).

Can you confirm whether FinPay has a PO on file for this period and whether your procurement team would be open to discussing a commit to avoid future retroactive true-ups? I'll aim to get you an internal proposal by end of day Friday.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Invoice question: unexpected overage on 2026-02-28 invoice

Forwarding FinPay's note and the usage export. Key facts: invoice is $42,150; they say they were not expecting a retroactive true-up.

Options I'm considering:
- Uphold the invoice as-written (per Standard EULA addendum: retroactive true-ups at list rates) — this is clean but may sour the account.
- Offer a one-time credit (we've done 20–35% on a case-by-case basis) to preserve ARR and upsell opportunity.
- Convert the overage into a committed capacity addendum that would translate the $42k into n months of reserved capacity at a negotiated rate.

Proposed customer-facing approach: present two pathways — (A) Immediate adjusted invoice reflecting one-time credit leaving a smaller balance due, or (B) move the amount into a 12-month reserved addendum (monthly charge) if they sign the addendum within 14 days.

Numbers (rough):
- Invoice gross: $42,150
- 30% credit: $12,645 (net due $29,505)
- Spread as 12-mo credit: $3,512.50/mo applied to future invoices, or we can apply a one-time reduction.

Requests:
1) Lauren — do we have precedent / approval to offer 30% credit here?
2) Stephanie — can finance issue an adjusted invoice and updated ledger if we approve the credit, and how fast can we deliver it?
3) Monica — CS to confirm product-side validity of usage report and whether any logging/retention issues contributed to this.

Attachments: FinPay_Q4_usage_export.csv; Inv_2026-02-28.pdf; SOW-FinPay-Addendum.docx (draft)

Thanks,
Rafael

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Invoice question: unexpected overage on 2026-02-28 invoice

Rafael — I agree we should avoid an all-or-nothing posture. Precedent: for strategic mid-market accounts we have given up to 30% credit on one-time true-ups when there's a clear path to an upsell or committed capacity.

My recommendation: offer 25% credit immediately (less aggressive than 30% but within margin), and simultaneously present a conversion path: if FinPay signs the 12-month committed addendum at an additional $10,000/month (effective 1 Apr 2026), apply the remaining value as a 9-month credit on next invoices.

Please proceed with the following:
- Stephanie: prepare an adjusted invoice showing the 25% credit and an alternate DocuSign addendum for the commit route.
- Rafael/CS: propose timeline to FinPay and ask for PO confirmation.

I'll greenlight any write-off below 20% but want finance to prepare the adjusted billing at 25% pending their review.

Lauren
VP, Commercial

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@finpay.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finpay.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invoice question: unexpected overage on 2026-02-28 invoice

Hi Ayesha / Marcus — thanks for your patience while we reviewed this. Summary and next steps: 

1) We validated the usage export against our logs — the $42,150 charge is a true retrospective adjustment for Q4 usage that fell outside the committed capacity in your existing plan.

2) To resolve this quickly and preserve our partnership, Redwood will offer an adjusted settlement: a 25% one-time credit against Inv_2026-02-28 (credit = $10,537.50), leaving a net balance of $31,612.50.

3) If FinPay prefers to avoid a one-time payment, we can convert the net balance into a 12-month committed addendum. Example: additional $10,000/month committed capacity starting 2026-04-01; we would apply the remaining balance as a monthly credit over the first 9 months of the new agreement.

4) Attached for signature: SOW-FinPay-Addendum.docx (draft) via DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/FinPay-RDW-addendum-2026. Also attached is an adjusted invoice stub: Inv_2026-02-28-adjusted.pdf and the original usage export.

Please confirm whether you would like the adjusted invoice issued (net $31,612.50) or whether you'd prefer the conversion path. If converting, please indicate the approver and PO for the addendum so finance can finalize the DocuSign envelope.

Next steps / timeline:
- You confirm path (Invoice or Commit) — within 3 business days.
- If Invoice: Redwood issues adjusted invoice; payment due per standard terms (Net 30).
- If Commit: we send DocuSign; once signed, finance will schedule monthly credits to start on the first invoice after the addendum activation.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you'd like to walk the numbers.

Best regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
r.mendes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186
Redwood Inference
